spot.description: Where in the garden the telescope stands (ty spot); null when none is named, and in the demo.

skyline_measured.description: Whether a measured skyline is in use for this spot; false means the windows go by the lowest altitude alone.

discovery.description: The discovery programmes (programmes/*.toml), the night's first purpose: each field's window in darkness above the horizon limits and measured skyline, best first; window null when it is not up in darkness.

minutes.description: For a mosaic, minutes on each panel.

panels.description: a mosaic's panel count (its grid); 1 for a single field

in_clear.description: The window cut to the forecast's clear spell; null when the field is not up while it is clear.

best_in_clear.description: When to take it: the best time inside the clear spell.

last_run.description: When the programme last imaged any of its fields (UTC), from its newest session with a picture or frames; null if never.

watch.description: The programme's dated events, each from a paper ([[watch]] in its file): whether tonight is inside one of its windows, and the next window.

window.description: Tonight's window, first and last day (UTC).

next.description: The next window after tonight, first and last day (UTC).

best_tonight.description: Up to five of the night's best targets (tonight.py's order) that fill a quarter of the frame's width or more, the size the person asked for on 14 October 2026; objects sharing one frame taken together (the Double Cluster); each with the share of the frame's width it fills, the mosaic grid it needs when bigger than the frame, and how often it has been imaged already (a new one is said as new, a repeat as adding to its stack).

what.description: What it is, from the catalogue alone (OpenNGC): its name, class, galaxy type, whether a disc is seen edge-on or face-on (from its axes), its size and magnitude.

frame_share.description: What it fills of the frame's width, at most 1: its length, or with others in the same frame their lengths added.

with.description: Others in the same frame, taken with it (NGC 884 with NGC 869, the Double Cluster); size_arcmin is then the span from the far edge of one to the far edge of the other.

panels.description: Columns x rows of the smallest mosaic that covers it (mosaic.py), null when one frame does.

other_fields.description: Galaxies up in darkness tonight, 8 arcmin or larger, whose centres lie in no discovery programme's frame (the camera's rectangle, footprint.py): fresh patrol fields, ranked by value: searchable tonight (a usable reference kept) or not (half), days since watched up to 20 (a supernova stays near its peak about three weeks), the share of the galaxy the frame holds, and the planner's score. field is what to patrol (a kept reference's field when the galaxy lies in its frame); reference false means tonight's stack becomes the reference and only later nights are searched; supernova names a bright one listed in it now, which the reference will then contain; why gives the reasons in words.

days_since_watched.description: Since the field's newest session; null if never.

what.description: What it is, from the catalogue alone (OpenNGC): its name, class, galaxy type, whether a disc is seen edge-on or face-on (from its axes), its size and magnitude.

supernovae.description: Supernovae on the Rochester list of active ones, brighter than magnitude 15.5 when last measured in the past 30 days, that are up here in the dark tonight; brightest first. Empty offline and in the demo.

id.description: SN and its name, e.g. SN 2026aaiv.

last_seen.description: The date of that magnitude, YYYY-MM-DD.

campaigns.description: Variable stars the AAVSO Target Tool lists (its alerts, campaigns and sections) that this camera can measure tonight: photometry in V or any filter, a range within reach, up in the dark here. AAVSO's high-priority ones first, then the most overdue. Empty without a Target Tool key, and in the demo.

section.description: The Target Tool's section(s): Alerts / Campaigns, cataclysmic variables and so on.

days_since_measured.description: Days since anyone's last measurement reached AAVSO.

overdue.description: days_since_measured over cadence_days: above 1, a measurement is overdue.

papers.description: arXiv's papers not yet marked read (literature.py --read) on each topic watched, however old (literature.py: Tabby's star, novae in M31 and M33, dipping stars, technosignatures and SETI, transit timing), only topics with any. To read, not results. Empty in the demo.

research.description: The research that needs no sky, in the night's terms (agent.research_tonight): the leads waiting and to ask again, how many are unexplained, the papers unread, each survey's coverage, the most intriguing leads looked into (investigate.py --summary's order), and observe_tonight: those this telescope can watch, still unsettled, up in tonight's dark hours, each with a dry-run GoTo; next_waiting: the next leads investigate.py will look into, each with why it was flagged. error when a record could not be read. Empty in the demo.

recommendation.description: What to do with tonight's clear spell, from now, in order (agent.recommend): it starts at the later of the clear spell's start and now, plus agent.SETUP_MINUTES when the telescope is not set up (ready false: no plate solve in the last hour), and on a marginal night leaves agent.SLACK of the spell unplanned. A programme inside a watch window tonight first, then a second look at a candidate seen on more than one night (one mosaic panel alone, agent.FOLLOW_MINUTES), then a research lead up tonight, then the programmes as their fields come best, each only if it can finish in the clear time left with patrol.OVERHEAD per field or panel for the GoTo and plate solve (a mosaic takes the panels that fit); with fog forecast a brightness measurement is left out unless a watch window makes tonight count. left_out says why each other one is not taken; note is set when no clear spell is forecast.

from.description: When the plan can start (local time, ISO 8601).

ready.description: Whether the telescope is set up now (a plate solve in the last hour).

alternatives.description: Big targets up in the plan's time, the other choice to the patrols: what, about, size, best, new.

sources.description: Each outside feed this answer used, and how old its data is: fresh (fetched now), cached (a copy kept within max_age_hours), stale (an older copy, kept because the source failed: not tonight's data) or unavailable. Empty in the demo.

fetched.description: UTC, ISO 8601: when the data was fetched from the source.

news.description: The sky's events from today to four days ahead (in-the-sky.org), in date order, then astronomy headlines of the last two days (Universe Today, the BAA), newest first. Empty offline and in the demo.

when.description: UTC, ISO 8601: the event's day, or when the headline was published.
